It is about: researcher Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292).

Claims:
1. Morphological analysis and tagging of Serbian and other Slavic languages using finite-state and statistical methods. [SYN-PUB-03633, SYN-PUB-03638, SYN-PUB-03641]
2. Cross-lingual transfer learning for NLP tasks across typologically distant language pairs, including Serbian–Hungarian and Serbian–Macedonian. [SYN-PUB-03635, SYN-PUB-03640, SYN-PRJ-0545]
3. Corpus design, annotation scheme development, and inter-annotator agreement measurement for linguistic phenomena including syntax, aspect, morphology, and information structure. [SYN-PUB-03634, SYN-PUB-03639, SYN-PUB-03644, SYN-PRJ-0544]
4. Named entity recognition and annotation transfer for low-resource languages using projection methods and weak supervision. [SYN-PUB-03640]
5. Dependency parsing and syntactic annotation for South Slavic languages using Universal Dependencies format and transition-based methods. [SYN-PUB-03637, SYN-PUB-03634]
6. Construction of morphological lexicons and inflectional resources for minority languages of Vojvodina including Pannonian Rusyn. [SYN-PUB-03641, SYN-PRJ-0544]
7. Domain-adaptive fine-tuning of multilingual transformer models for morphosyntactic tasks and low-resource language benchmarking. [SYN-PUB-03638, SYN-PUB-03643]
8. Historical text processing including sentence boundary detection in Church-Slavonic manuscripts and OCR post-processing. [SYN-PUB-03642]
9. Served as linguistic consultant to a Novi Sad software localisation company during 2017–2018 on Serbian morphological requirements for terminology management. [R0292]
10. Open to contract research on corpus annotation and data preparation for Serbian and regional languages. [R0292]
11. Open to consulting on NLP pipeline development for South Slavic or Finno-Ugric language inputs. [R0292]
12. Open to supervision of industrial PhD students in multilingual text processing. [R0292]
13. Was on leave until September 2024. [R…[+23278 chars]

Review the claims of pair C003-CH4:R0283.
It is about: researcher Ana Mamužić (R0283) and company AutomVoj a.d. (C003), challenge C003-CH4.

Claims:
1. AutomVoj suspects harmonic current emissions from SINAMICS frequency drives are disturbing precision instruments on the customer LV grid, and needs on-site measurement and a design rule to prevent recurrence (C003-CH4). [C003-CH4]
2. The researcher co-authored papers on conducted EMI measurement and characterisation using LISN-based testing and spectral analysis, and on differential-mode and common-mode noise separation in three-phase PWM drives (SYN-PUB-03540, SYN-PUB-03535). [SYN-PUB-03540, SYN-PUB-03535]
3. The researcher co-authored papers on EMC filter design and validation for variable-speed drives optimised for IEC 61800-3 Category C2 compliance, and on harmonic spectrum analysis in multi-drive systems (SYN-PUB-03536, SYN-PUB-03539, SYN-PUB-01738). [SYN-PUB-03536, SYN-PUB-03539, SYN-PUB-01738]
4. The researcher led project EMCDRIVE on EMC characterisation and filter validation for variable-speed drives in industrial environments, delivering a filter design procedure and a public dataset of emission spectra and protective earth impedance profiles (SYN-PRJ-0392). [SYN-PRJ-0392]
5. The researcher provided consulting to domestic manufacturers of industrial control panels on EMC filter selection and IEC 61800-3 pre-compliance testing procedures, and completed a contract audit of a regional drive assembler for Category C2 compliance (R0283). [R0283]
6. Review the claims of pair C003-CH4:R0611.
It is about: researcher Danijela Ninkov (R0611) and company AutomVoj a.d. (C003), challenge C003-CH4.

Claims:
1. AutomVoj needs harmonic emission measurement on its customer LV grid and identification of the drive configuration responsible, which requires LV network harmonic characterisation expertise (C003-CH4). [C003-CH4]
2. The researcher co-authored a paper on harmonic voltage distortion from variable-speed drives and harmonic load flow modelling in industrial low-voltage networks (SYN-PUB-07003). [SYN-PUB-07003]
3. The researcher co-authored papers on conducted emission characterisation of power electronic equipment using LISN methods and on common-mode and differential-mode separation of conducted emissions with uncertainty quantification (SYN-PUB-07008, SYN-PUB-07006). [SYN-PUB-07008, SYN-PUB-07006]

The researcher is open to contract research on electromagnetic compatibility characterisation of industrial power electronic equipment and pre-compliance conducted emission testing, and offers access to LISN-based conducted emission measurement and power quality class A monitoring equipment (R0611). [R0611]
5. Authors: Milan Petrović (R0925); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Dragan Vasiljević (outside co-author); Katarina Horvat (outside co-author).
This paper presents SrbBERT-Web, a transformer language model pre-trained from scratch on a large-scale crawl of Serbian web text comprising approximately 14 billion tokens. We describe the data collection and cleaning pipeline, which addresses noise specific to Serbian web content, including mixed-script documents, informal spelling variations, and code-switched passages. The model adopts a RoBERTa-style architecture and is trained with dynamic masking on deduplicated data. We evaluate SrbBERT-Web on four downstream tasks: named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, morphological tagging, and extractive question answering, comparing it against multilingual baselines such as mBERT and XLM-R, as well as against smaller domain-specific Serbian models. SrbBERT-Web consistently outperforms all baselines on three of the four tasks, with especially pronounced gains on question answering and sentiment analysis. Authors: Mónika Papp (R0524); Petra Szabó (outside co-author); Dragana Mirković (outside co-author).
Keywords: contrastive learning; sentence encoders; fine-tuning; legal NLP; medical NLP; low-resource.
Large multilingual sentence encoders trained on general web data often perform poorly on specialised domains where vocabulary and sentence structure differ substantially from general text. We investigate the effectiveness of contrastive fine-tuning—using in-domain positive pairs and hard negatives mined from the same corpus—when the available domain-specific parallel corpus is small (2,000–8,000 sentence pairs). Experiments cover two subdomains (legal and medical) and three language pairs (EN–SR, EN–HU, EN–RO). We compare full fine-tuning, adapter-based fine-tuning, and prompt-based fine-tuning on top of LaBSE and XLM-R-large. Adapter-based fine-tuning with hard-negative mining matches or exceeds full fine-tuning on all six subdomain–language-pair combinations while using 7% of the trainable parameters. Sources:
[SYN-PUB-03633] publication · Morphological Disambiguation in Serbian: A Maximum Entropy Approach on a Balanced News Corpus · 2011 · researchers R0292
Morphological Disambiguation in Serbian: A Maximum Entropy Approach on a Balanced News Corpus (2011, conference, Proceedings of the South Slavic Language Technology Workshop (SoLaT 2011), Ljubljana).
Authors: Aleksandar Vučković (outside co-author); Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292); Miroslava Tešić (outside co-author).
Keywords: morphological disambiguation; Serbian; maximum entropy; corpus annotation; MULTEXT-East.
This paper describes the construction and annotation of a 200,000-token Serbian newspaper corpus and the training of a maximum entropy morphological disambiguator on it. Serbian presents particular challenges for disambiguation due to its free word order, extensive inflectional paradigms, and syncretism across several case forms. The corpus was sampled from three regional dailies covering the period 2005–2009 and annotated manually by two linguists following an adapted MULTEXT-East tagset. Inter-annotator agreement reached κ = 0.87 on the full tagset. The maximum entropy model trained on 80% of the data achieved a per-token accuracy of 91.3% on the held-out test set, outperforming a rule-based baseline by 4.1 percentage points. Error analysis showed that the remaining errors cluster heavily around nominal case syncretism in neuter nouns and verbal aspect ambiguity. Review the claims of pair C006-CH1:R0484.
It is about: researcher Jovan Puzović (R0484) and company PravniPilot a.d. (C006), challenge C006-CH1.

Claims:
1. The challenge requires improving case-outcome prediction on a small labeled Serbian legal corpus where fine-tuned multilingual models have plateaued (C006-CH1). [C006-CH1]
2. Puzović co-authored work on classification and outcome prediction on imbalanced legal text datasets using resampling strategies and cost-sensitive learning objectives (SYN-PUB-05712, SYN-PUB-03940, SYN-PUB-05706). [SYN-PUB-05712, SYN-PUB-03940, SYN-PUB-05706]
3. Puzović co-authored work on synthetic legal text generation using conditional language models and back-translation for data augmentation, and evaluated synthetic data validity against domain expertise (SYN-PUB-05711, SYN-PUB-05710, SYN-PUB-05707). [SYN-PUB-05711, SYN-PUB-05710, SYN-PUB-05707]
4. Puzović co-authored work on transfer learning and intermediate pretraining strategies for adapting general language models to specialised legal domains on small datasets, and took part in a project covering corpus construction and named entity recognition for Serbian legal text (SYN-PUB-05708, SYN-PRJ-0554). [SYN-PUB-05708, SYN-PRJ-0554]
5. The published work covers legal text classification broadly; it is not confirmed to cover Serbian commercial-dispute court-decision formats specifically (SYN-PUB-05712, SYN-PUB-05708). [SYN-PUB-05712, SYN-PUB-05708]
6. The 12-month deadline (C006-CH1) is tight for validating that synthetic data improves real-world held-out accuracy rather than inflating training metrics. [C006-CH1]

Review the claims of pair C006-CH3:R0127.
It is about: researcher Emilija Tešić (R0127) and company PravniPilot a.d. (C006), challenge C006-CH3.

Claims:
1. The challenge requires sentence-level provenance and confidence scoring in a RAG system, a gap PravniPilot states it cannot solve internally (C006-CH3). [C006-CH3]
2. Tešić co-authored work on citation grounding and fact verification in retrieval-augmented generation systems with cross-encoder ranking (SYN-PUB-01678, SYN-PUB-01682). [SYN-PUB-01678, SYN-PUB-01682]
3. Tešić co-authored work on hallucination detection in language model outputs using atomic claim decomposition and natural language inference (SYN-PUB-01679, SYN-PUB-01675). [SYN-PUB-01679, SYN-PUB-01675]
4. Tešić collaborated with a regional legal information provider during the VERIFAI-RS project, advising on requirements and evaluating prototype verification modules against real workflows (SYN-PRJ-0556). [SYN-PRJ-0556]
5. The published work covers citation grounding in RAG systems generally; the records do not show work on South Slavic or multilingual legal corpora specifically. [SYN-PUB-01678, SYN-PUB-01682]
6. SYN-PUB-01682 covers real-time claim verification with latency budgets for document assistant systems, but the records do not specify whether the tested latency budgets match the production constraints of PravniPilot's stack. [SYN-PUB-01682, C006-CH3]

Sources:
[C006-CH3] challenge · Law firm users copy our AI-generated research summaries directly into briefs without reading them, and twice this year the summaries contained an outdated precedent; we need a way to attach confidence scores and source provenance to every generated sentence. · company C006

It is about: researcher Milan Petrović (R0925) and company PravniPilot a.d. (C006), challenge C006-CH3.

3. [C006-CH3, SYN-PUB-09810, SYN-PUB-09805, SYN-PUB-09809]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-09810] publication · Retrieval-augmented generation for Serbian: adapting RAG pipelines to a morphologically rich language · 2024 · researchers R0925

Authors: Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Stefan Novaković (outside co-author); Milan Petrović (R0925).

Review the claims of pair C006-CH3:R0524.
It is about: researcher Mónika Papp (R0524) and company PravniPilot a.d. (C006), challenge C006-CH3.

Claims:
1. The challenge requires confidence scoring and factual preservation checks on multilingual legal summaries, a gap PravniPilot states explicitly (C006-CH3). [C006-CH3]
2. Papp co-authored work on evaluation of hallucination and factual preservation in cross-lingual summarisation by instruction-tuned large language models on structured documents (SYN-PUB-06160). [SYN-PUB-06160]
3. Papp co-authored work on cross-lingual sentence embeddings and semantic similarity for legal and administrative documents using transformer models such as LaBSE and XLM-R (SYN-PUB-06159, SYN-PUB-06158, SYN-PUB-06155). [SYN-PUB-06159, SYN-PUB-06158, SYN-PUB-06155]
4. Papp co-authored work on construction and evaluation of multilingual semantic textual similarity benchmarks and cross-lingual NLP resources for South Slavic languages (SYN-PUB-06154). [SYN-PUB-06154]
5. Develop and benchmark cross-lingual sentence-level semantic similarity and factual-preservation evaluation for PravniPilot's summaries of court decisions in Serbian, Croatian and Bosnian, using multilingual transformer models and cross-lingual benchmarks adapted to the legal domain (C006-CH3, SYN-PUB-06160, SYN-PUB-06159, SYN-PUB-06154). [C006-CH3, SYN-PUB-06160, SYN-PUB-06159, SYN-PUB-06154]
6. SYN-PUB-06160 covers hallucination evaluation in cross-lingual summarisation; the records do not show work on the RAG citation grounding or source-link attribution pipeline that C006-CH3 requires as the primary output. [SYN-PUB-06160, C006-CH3]
7. Papp's records on legal documents cover Serbian, Hungarian and Romanian language pairs; the records do not show specific coverage of Croatian or Bosnian legal text. [SYN-PUB-06159, SYN-PUB-06158]

data.message:
Review the claims of pair C006-CH1:R0925.
It is about: researcher Milan Petrović (R0925) and company PravniPilot a.d. (C006), challenge C006-CH1.

Claims:
1. Petrović co-authored work on pre-training transformer language models on Serbian web text with mixed-script handling (SYN-PUB-09804). [SYN-PUB-09804]
2. Petrović and PravniPilot would apply cross-lingual transfer learning across Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian court decisions — using shared subword vocabularies and morphology-aware tokenisation — to improve the base representation used by the case-outcome classifier trained on the company's 9,000 labeled decisions (C006-CH1, SYN-PUB-09809, SYN-PUB-09812). [C006-CH1, SYN-PUB-09809, SYN-PUB-09812]
3. Petrović took part in the SRB-NLP project, which runs from 2023 to 2026, overlapping with the 12-month engagement the challenge requires (SYN-PRJ-0009, C006-CH1). [SYN-PRJ-0009, C006-CH1]

Sources:
[C006-CH1] challenge · Our case-outcome prediction model achieves only 61% accuracy on commercial-dispute rulings from Serbian courts, which is barely better than a lawyer's gut feeling; we suspect the problem is that our training set has only 9,000 labelled decisions and courts don't publish enough structured data. · company C006
Our case-outcome prediction model achieves only 61% accuracy on commercial-dispute rulings from Serbian courts, which is barely better than a lawyer's gut feeling; we suspect the problem is that our training set has only 9,000 labelled decisions and courts don't publish enough structured data.

Our prediction model was trained on roughly 9,000 labeled commercial-dispute decisions from Serbian courts. At 61% accuracy it is not meaningfully better than what an experienced lawyer estimates from memory. We have tried basic data augmentation and have experimented with pre-trained multilingual models fine-tuned on our corpus, but neither moved the needle past 63% in internal tests. The core problem is data volume: Serbian courts do not publish decisions…[+7098 chars]

EMCDRIVE: EMC Characterisation and Filter Validation Methods for SiC-Based Variable-Speed Drives in Industrial Environments (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0283 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš; Institute for Power Engineering and Automation, Subotica.
The project addressed the gap between laboratory IEC 61800-3 compliance and field performance of EMC filters for SiC MOSFET motor drives. The work covered three main activities: systematic conducted emission characterisation of SiC drives from 2.2 kW to 22 kW, development of a measurement uncertainty budget specific to high-di/dt inverter systems, and design and experimental validation of filter topologies robust to realistic PE impedance variation encountered in Serbian industrial installations. Forty-seven sites were surveyed for PE impedance. Deliverables included a filter design procedure, a dataset of emission spectra and PE impedance profiles made publicly available, and two validated simulation models. The project supported two PhD students and produced eight peer-reviewed publications.

Selective Harmonic Elimination Under Unbalanced DC-Link Voltages in Cascaded H-Bridge Inverters: Reformulation and Experimental Validation (2026, journal, IET Power Electronics).
Authors: Zorica Jovanović (R0567); Stefan Lukić (outside co-author); Claudia Ferrero (outside co-author); Dragan Milić (outside co-author).
Keywords: unbalanced DC link; SHE-PWM reformulation; cascaded H-bridge; harmonic correction; photovoltaic drive.
Standard SHE-PWM formulations assume equal DC-link voltages across all H-bridge cells. In practice, unequal charging of isolated DC sources—common in photovoltaic-fed or battery-buffered CHB drives—distorts the output voltage spectrum and invalidates pre-computed angle tables. This paper reformulates the SHE-PWM equations to account for arbitrary, known DC-link voltage imbalances across a seven-level (three-cell) CHB inverter. The reformulated system is solved using a trust-region algorithm with multiple random starting points to locate all physically meaningful solution branches. Angle correction maps were constructed for DC-link voltage deviations of up to ±15% relative to nominal. Our case-outcome prediction model achieves only 61% accuracy on commercial-dispute rulings from Serbian courts, which is barely better than a lawyer's gut feeling; we suspect the problem is that our training set has only 9,000 labelled decisions and courts don't publish enough structured data.

Our prediction model was trained on roughly 9,000 labeled commercial-dispute decisions from Serbian courts. At 61% accuracy it is not meaningfully better than what an experienced lawyer estimates from memory. We have tried basic data augmentation and have experimented with pre-trained multilingual models fine-tuned on our corpus, but neither moved the needle past 63% in internal tests. The core problem is data volume: Serbian courts do not publish decisions in a consistent machine-readable format, so each document requires significant cleaning before it can be labeled. We have one full-time data engineer and two part-time annotators working on this. We estimate we need at least 40,000 clean, labeled decisions to reach accuracy worth advertising. We are open to exploring transfer learning from Croatian or Bosnian court data, semi-supervised labeling, or better feature extraction from judgment text. Benchmarking Counterfactual Explanation Methods for Tabular Classifiers: A Comparative Study (2017, book chapter, Advances in Explainable and Trustworthy Machine Learning (edited volume, Springer Verlag)).
Authors: Miroslav Stanić (outside co-author); Emilija Tešić (R0127); Tobias Brendel (outside co-author).
Keywords: counterfactual explanations; XAI benchmarking; tabular data; actionability; DICE.
Counterfactual explanations describe the minimal feature changes needed to obtain a different classifier output. This chapter surveys and benchmarks eight counterfactual generation methods on six tabular datasets spanning finance, healthcare, and public administration. Evaluation covers proximity (mean feature distance to the original instance), sparsity (average number of changed features), validity (fraction of counterfactuals that achieve the target class), and actionability (fraction respecting domain-defined immutable features). Methods tested include DICE, a growing spheres approach, a prototype-based method, and five research implementations. No single method dominates across all criteria: prototype-based approaches score highest on actionability (0.84) but lowest on proximity. Growing spheres produce the sparsest counterfactuals (1.9 changed features on average) but have lower validity for nonlinear boundaries. Our case-outcome prediction model achieves only 61% accuracy on commercial-dispute rulings from Serbian courts, which is barely better than a lawyer's gut feeling; we suspect the problem is that our training set has only 9,000 labelled decisions and courts don't publish enough structured data.

Our prediction model was trained on roughly 9,000 labeled commercial-dispute decisions from Serbian courts. At 61% accuracy it is not meaningfully better than what an experienced lawyer estimates from memory. We have tried basic data augmentation and have experimented with pre-trained multilingual models fine-tuned on our corpus, but neither moved the needle past 63% in internal tests. The core problem is data volume: Serbian courts do not publish decisions in a consistent machine-readable format, so each document requires significant cleaning before it can be labeled. We have one full-time data engineer and two part-time annotators working on this. We estimate we need at least 40,000 clean, labeled decisions to reach accuracy worth advertising. The failure mechanism combines low-temperature thermal cycling, condensation, and cyclic vibration at the crossmember-to-stringer weld joint in mild steel frames. Review the claims of proposal C003-CH1-R0365.
It is about: researcher Bojan Erić (R0365) and company AutomVoj a.d. (C003), challenge C003-CH1.

Claims:
1. AutomVoj a.d. works in robotics and industrial automation. [C003]
2. Bojan Erić is an Associate Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering (Machine Design and Mechanics), Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0365]
3. Mild steel conveyor frames crack at crossmember-to-stringer weld joints after roughly 18 months of continuous operation in food-processing cold stores at 2–6 °C, and AutomVoj has replaced 14 assemblies under warranty this year. [C003-CH1]
4. Room-temperature static and cyclic loading tests have not reproduced the failure, indicating that low-temperature thermal cycling, condensation, and vibration interact to drive crack initiation. [C003-CH1]
5. The company has photographs, measurements from site visits, and two failed frame sections with visible weld cracks available for investigation. [C003-CH1]
6. A 2024 study reports that the crack growth rate of welded steel joints in a corrosive environment is higher than that of base metal, driven by residual stress and high dislocation density in the heat-affected zone. [W4402945203]
7. Two failed frame sections with weld cracks, photographs, and measurements from site visits, available for laboratory inspection. [C003-CH1]
8. Historical design records, welding procedure, filler material specification, and corrosion-protection specification for the affected frames. [C003-CH1]
9. In-house fabrication shop with welding capability to produce reference and candidate weld-joint specimens to any revised procedure. [C003]
10. Access to customer cold-store installations operating at 2–6 °C, including vibration measurements taken during site visits. [C003-CH1, C003/news/2024-04-03/AutomVoj Delivers Sorting Line to Kovačević Frozen Foods in Hungary]

Review the claims of pair C004-CH1:R0364.
It is about: researcher Žarko Pejić (R0364) and company OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004), challenge C004-CH1.

Claims:
1. OsiguroMi's contractual threshold must not be replaced but corrected through spatially accurate parcel-level rainfall estimates derived from a sparse gauge network and satellite data. [C004-CH1]

4. Pejić provided technical consultancy to an agricultural insurance intermediary in 2023 on spatial resolution requirements for parametric rainfall products. [R0364]
5. Pejić leads the AGRIDATA-CROSS cross-border project on meteorological data infrastructure and climate risk assessment serving agricultural stakeholders. [SYN-PRJ-0113]
6. Using OsiguroMi's 140-station network and satellite products, Žarko Pejić would build a kriging-with-external-drift precipitation downscaling model to produce parcel-scale rainfall grids, validate them against the available gauge records, and run burn-analysis-based calibration of the contractual payout trigger for the coming season. [C004-CH1, SYN-PUB-04461, SYN-PUB-04462, SYN-PUB-04014, SYN-PUB-04460]
7. The publications on multi-source bias correction cover ERA5, IMERG, and TMPA; coverage of the specific private agro-meteorological networks OsiguroMi holds is not documented in the record. [SYN-PUB-04014, SYN-PUB-04464, SYN-PUB-04463]
8. The company's target timeline is six to nine months; burn analysis and trigger recalibration across parcel scale may require multi-season historical depth not yet confirmed in the available datasets. [C004]

4. Using OsiguroMi's 140-station network and satellite covariates, Milutin Đukić would apply regression-kriging and satellite downscaling to interpolate precipitation to parcel scale, producing corrected rainfall grids that OsiguroMi can use to recalibrate its payout thresholds. [C004-CH1, SYN-PUB-08102, SYN-PUB-08100, SYN-PUB-08095, SYN-PUB-08093]

It is about: researcher Snežana Todorović (R0741) and company PravniPilot a.d. (C006), challenge C006-CH4.

data.message:
Review the claims of pair C004-CH1:R0727.
It is about: researcher Milutin Đukić (R0727) and company OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004), challenge C004-CH1.

Claims:
1. Đukić co-authored a publication on geostatistical interpolation of sparse climate station networks using variogram estimation and kriging for precipitation. [SYN-PUB-08102]
2. Đukić co-authored publications on spatial downscaling of satellite and reanalysis data to produce high-resolution grids of agroclimatic variables including air temperature and growing degree days. [SYN-PUB-08094, SYN-PUB-08093]
3. Using OsiguroMi's 140-station network and satellite covariates, Milutin Đukić would apply regression-kriging and satellite downscaling to interpolate precipitation to parcel scale, producing corrected rainfall grids that OsiguroMi can use to calibrate payout logic without replacing the contractual threshold. [C004-CH1, SYN-PUB-08102, SYN-PUB-08094, SYN-PUB-08093]
4. Among Đukić's interpolation publications, SYN-PUB-08102 covers precipitation alongside temperature and ET₀; the remaining documented interpolation work covers temperature and ET₀. [SYN-PUB-08102, SYN-PUB-08098, SYN-PUB-08095, SYN-PUB-08093]

Sources:
[C004-CH1] challenge · Our weather-triggered crop parametric product pays out when measured rainfall at the nearest official station drops below a threshold, but farmers tell us the station is sometimes 30 km away and their field got rain while the station recorded drought — we're paying out when we shouldn't and refusing when we should. · company C004

Review the claims of profile R0127.
It is about: researcher Emilija Tešić (R0127).

Claims:
1. Led the VERIFAI-RS project, which included a regional legal information provider as an observer partner and developed a prototype verification module for AI-generated text. [SYN-PRJ-0556]

Sources:
[SYN-PRJ-0556] project · Verification and Explanation of AI-Generated Text in High-Stakes Domains · 2021 · researchers R0127
VERIFAI-RS: Verification and Explanation of AI-Generated Text in High-Stakes Domains (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0127 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Organisational Sciences, University of Belgrade; Department of Computer Science, University of Pécs; Regional Legal Information Centre Novi Sad (observer partner).
The project investigated automated fact verification and explanation methods for AI-generated text with a focus on legal, medical, and financial documents in Serbian and English. The team built annotated corpora for hallucination detection, developed lightweight NLI models fine-tuned on domain-specific data, and designed a modular verification pipeline applicable to retrieval-augmented generation architectures. The project funded two PhD students and supported collaboration with the Faculty of Organisational Sciences, University of Belgrade, and the University of Pécs. Outputs include three datasets released under open licences, seven peer-reviewed publications, and a prototype verification module tested with a regional legal information provider.

Review the claims of profile R0217.
It is about: researcher Andrea Malešević (R0217).

Claims:
1. Adaptive partitioning strategies for certificate revocation databases in Apache Cassandra accommodating variable issuance rates. [SYN-PUB-02773]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-02773] publication · Adaptivno particionisanje vremenskih serija u bazama podataka za revokaciju sertifikata sa promenljivim stopama izdavanja · 2026 · researchers R0217
Adaptivno particionisanje vremenskih serija u bazama podataka za revokaciju sertifikata sa promenljivim stopama izdavanja (2026, journal, Journal of Data Engineering and Distributed Systems).
Authors: Andrea Malešević (R0217); Tamara Bošnjak (outside co-author); Nemanja Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: adaptive partitioning; time series; certificate revocation; Apache Cassandra; dynamic sharding.
Sistemi za revokaciju sertifikata u savremenim mrežama suočavaju se s visokim i neravnomernim stopama izdavanja koje otežavaju statičke strategije particionisanja. Ovaj rad predlaže shemu adaptivnog particionisanja zasnovanog na praćenju gustine zapisa po vremenskom prozoru i automatskom deljenju particija kada gustina premaši konfigurabilni prag. Implementacija je realizovana kao proširenje iznad Apache Cassandre i evaluirana je na sintetičkim skupovima podataka koji modeluju rast od 1.000 do 50.000 novih sertifikata na dan tokom perioda od godinu dana. Mereni su vreme upita, balans particija i troškovi reparticionisanja. Adaptivna shema smanjuje maksimalno odstupanje veličine particija sa 340% na 28% u poređenju sa statičkim mesečnim particionisanjem, uz prosečni troškak reparticionisanja od 1,4 sekunde po operaciji deljenja na testnom klasteru. Rad takođe analizira ponašanje sheme pri naglim skokovima broja vydatih sertifikata.

Review the claims of profile R0349.
It is about: researcher Stefan Dragić (R0349).

Claims:
1. Design of inverted index structures using phoneme-based canonicalization to handle mixed-script text. [SYN-PUB-04278]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-04278] publication · Izgradnja invertovanog indeksa za srpske tekstove sa mešovitim pismom: osnovna metodologija · 2010 · researchers R0349
Izgradnja invertovanog indeksa za srpske tekstove sa mešovitim pismom: osnovna metodologija (2010, conference, Zbornik radova Konferencije o primeni računara i interneta u Srbiji (PRIS 2010)).
Authors: Milena Kovačević (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349).
Keywords: invertovani indeks; mešovito pismo; normalizacija; srpski jezik.
U radu se opisuje metodologija izgradnje invertovanog indeksa koji istovremeno obrađuje ćirilična i latinična pojavljivanja srpskih reči bez prethodnog potpunog prevođenja u jedno pismo. Predloženi postupak uključuje korak normalizacije tokena kojim se za svaki token generiše kanonska forma zasnovana na fonemskoj reprezentaciji, a zatim se fonemski ključevi koriste kao primarni identifikatori u indeksu. Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na korpusu od 120 000 novinskih članaka preuzetih iz tri srpska dnevna lista u periodu 2000–2008. Mere preciznosti i odziva upoređene su s dva bazična sistema koji koriste isključivo ćirilični, odnosno isključivo latinični indeks. Predloženi sistem postiže F1 vrednost od 0,81 u zadatku ad-hoc pretrage, što je povećanje od 14 procentnih poena u odnosu na bolji od dva bazična sistema. Rad takođe razmatra pitanje memorijskog otiska hibridnog indeksa i predlaže strategiju kompresije rečnika.

It is about: researcher Bojan Erić (R0365) and company AutomVoj a.d. (C003), challenge C003-CH1.

Claims:
1. Photographs and measurements of cracked joints collected during site visits to cold-store installations operating at 2–6 °C. [C003-CH1]

Sources:
[C003-CH1] challenge · Our conveyor frames crack at the weld joints after roughly 18 months of operation in chilled environments; we've replaced 14 assemblies under warranty this year and we can't reproduce the failure in our workshop because we test at room temperature. · company C003
Our conveyor frames crack at the weld joints after roughly 18 months of operation in chilled environments; we've replaced 14 assemblies under warranty this year and we can't reproduce the failure in our workshop because we test at room temperature.

Our conveyor frames are welded from mild steel hollow section and painted for corrosion resistance before delivery. When these systems run in customer cold stores — typically operating between 2 °C and 6 °C — we are seeing weld joint cracking at the main crossmember-to-stringer connections after about 18 months of continuous use. This year alone we have replaced 14 complete frame assemblies under warranty, which is costing us in material, travel, and lost engineer time. The frustrating part is that we have tried to reproduce the failure in our workshop and cannot do it. We test frames under load at room temperature and they pass without any problem. Our suspicion is that the combination of thermal cycling, condensation, and the vibration load from loaded belts is doing something we are not seeing at ambient conditions. We have photos and measurements of the cracked joints from site visits, and we still have two of the failed sections in storage. We do not currently have the equipment or know-how to test at low temperatures under cyclic load. Review the claims of profile R0261.
It is about: researcher Pavol Struhár (R0261).

Claims:
1. Bayesian change-point detection in high-frequency time series with autocorrelated noise and missing observations using particle filters. [SYN-PUB-03295]
2. Gaussian process regression for irregular and sparse sensor data with kernel selection and risk scoring in agricultural systems. [SYN-PUB-03301]
3. Sequential Bayesian updating of remaining useful life models for rotating equipment under concept drift using importance weighting. [SYN-PUB-03304]
4. Hierarchical Bayesian Poisson–Gamma models for failure rate heterogeneity across industrial machine populations with MCMC inference. [SYN-PUB-03297]
5. Extreme-value theory for transient phenomena in monitored systems, including GEV distribution fitting and return-level estimation with spatial correlation. [SYN-PUB-03298]
6. Online stochastic variational inference for streaming sensor anomaly detection using Dirichlet process mixtures deployable on edge devices. [SYN-PUB-03300]
7. Probabilistic load forecasting for individual industrial consumers using Bayesian quantile regression on smart meter data. [SYN-PUB-03302]
8. Actuarial pricing using telematics and sensor features through credibility theory embedded in Bayesian linear models. [SYN-PUB-03299]
9. Open to joint projects with companies generating high-frequency sensor or telematics data, contract research on probabilistic risk and pricing models, industrial PhD supervision, and consulting on Bayesian model design and validation. [R0261]
10. Provided statistical consulting to a regional property insurer during 2019–2020 on sensor-based premium adjustment for commercial fire risk. [R0261]
11. Led a Science Fund project developing modular software for ingesting IoT streams and fitting hierarchical Bayesian risk models with three SME collaborators in Vojvodina. [SYN-PRJ-0100]
12. He is not on sabbatical and has no planned leave through 2027. [R0261]

Review the claims of profile R0071.
It is about: researcher Olivera Rakić (R0071).

Claims:
1. Self-training with uncertainty filtering for semi-supervised anomaly detection in high-dimensional process data. [SYN-PUB-00962]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-00962] publication · Self-Training with Uncertainty Filtering for Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection in High-Dimensional Process Data · 2021 · researchers R0071
Self-Training with Uncertainty Filtering for Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection in High-Dimensional Process Data (2021, journal, Expert Systems with Applications and Engineering).
Authors: Miroslav Stanić (outside co-author); Sanja Kovačević (outside co-author); Olivera Rakić (R0071).
Keywords: self-training; pseudo-labelling; Monte Carlo dropout; uncertainty estimation; semi-supervised learning.
Self-training iteratively assigns pseudo-labels to unlabelled samples and retrains a classifier, but in highly imbalanced settings pseudo-label noise disproportionately corrupts the minority class. This paper introduces an uncertainty filter based on prediction entropy estimated through Monte Carlo dropout: only samples whose entropy falls below a calibrated threshold enter the pseudo-labelled pool. The method is tested on three high-dimensional datasets (128 to 512 features) derived from chemical reactor sensors, semiconductor fabrication metrology, and server performance counters, all with imbalance ratios above 1:300. Starting from 2% labelled data, the filtered self-training approach reaches 91% of fully supervised F1 performance on the chemical reactor dataset, compared to 74% for standard self-training. Runtime scales linearly in dataset size and does not require architectural changes beyond enabling dropout at inference time. A sensitivity analysis over the entropy threshold is provided.

Bayesian updating of catastrophe loss models using sequential Monte Carlo (2023, journal, Computational Statistics and Data Analysis).
Authors: Marija Ivanović-Pešić (outside co-author); László Varga (outside co-author); Péter Szabó (R0842).
Keywords: sequential Monte Carlo; Bayesian updating; catastrophe modelling; GPD; hailstorm losses.
Catastrophe risk models for pricing and reserving are typically calibrated on datasets that are augmented by a new large event every several years. Re-running full MCMC after each such update is computationally costly. We adapt a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) scheme to propagate posterior distributions over GPD parameters as new catastrophe event observations arrive. Tempering schedules and resampling strategies are tuned for the low-event-count regime typical of natural catastrophe lines: 8 to 30 historical events. We apply the SMC scheme to a stylised hailstorm loss series for the Pannonian Plain region, simulating sequential arrival of one to three new events. Review the claims of proposal C006-CH1-R0484.
It is about: researcher Jovan Puzović (R0484) and company PravniPilot a.d. (C006), challenge C006-CH1.

Claims:
1. PravniPilot a.d. works in legal tech. [C006]
2. Jovan Puzović is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0484]
3. A case-outcome prediction model trained on roughly 9,000 labeled Serbian commercial-dispute decisions achieves 61% accuracy and has plateaued near 63% despite basic data augmentation and fine-tuned multilingual pre-trained models. [C006-CH1]
4. The company estimates it needs at least 40,000 clean labeled decisions to reach the target 75% accuracy, but Serbian courts do not publish decisions in a consistent machine-readable format, making it hard to scale the labeled corpus without substantial manual effort. [C006-CH1]
5. PravniPilot must reach 75% accuracy on a held-out test set within 12 months to market the prediction feature with honest confidence intervals. [C006-CH1]

Tail Risk Estimation for Cloud Service Outage Losses: A Spliced Distribution Approach with Application to Serbian Fintech Firms (2026, preprint, Preprint, SSRN Working Paper Series).
Authors: Nikola Savić (outside co-author); Milica Đorđević (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422); Rita Bálint (R0970); Emilija Ostojić (R0671).
Keywords: spliced distribution; cloud outage; generalised Pareto; fintech; business interruption.
Cloud service outages generate bimodal loss profiles: a large mass of short, low-cost interruptions and a thin tail of prolonged outages with severe financial consequences. This paper fits spliced distributions combining a gamma body with a generalised Pareto tail to hourly downtime cost data collected from 19 fintech firms operating in Serbia between 2021 and 2024, yielding 2 641 outage episodes. The splice point is selected by minimising the integrated squared error between the empirical CDF and the fitted spliced distribution, resulting in an optimal threshold at the 87th empirical percentile. Keywords: vine copulas; R-vine; river discharge; multivariate flood risk; Danube.
Multivariate flood risk assessment requires joint models for discharge at several gauging stations simultaneously. An R-vine structure was selected using the minimum spanning tree algorithm applied to pairwise empirical Kendall τ values. Each pair copula family was chosen from a candidate set of twelve families by the Akaike information criterion. Applying Isolation Forest to Multivariate Numeric Anomalies in High-Frequency API Telemetry (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Data Quality in Engineering Systems (DQES 2021)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Luka Todorović (outside co-author); Péter Kovács (outside co-author).
Keywords: Isolation Forest; multivariate anomaly detection; IoT telemetry; streaming data; unsupervised learning.
High-frequency telemetry streams produced by IoT gateways and industrial APIs exhibit multivariate numeric patterns that rule-based detectors handle poorly when anomalies involve correlated deviations across several fields simultaneously. This paper investigates the use of the Isolation Forest algorithm for unsupervised anomaly detection in such streams, focusing on tuning the contamination parameter and the number of estimators under streaming constraints. Experiments used telemetry data from a factory automation pilot comprising six sensor channels sampled at 10 Hz over 30 days, yielding approximately 15.5 million records. Isolation Forest outperformed a univariate z-score baseline by 18 percentage points in F1 score on held-out labelled anomaly windows. The paper also reports the effect of sub-sampling strategies on detection quality when full-stream processing is not feasible, and provides a reference configuration table for practitioners operating within defined memory budgets. Review the claims of pair C004-CH2:R1020.
It is about: researcher Predrag Nedić (R1020) and company OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004), challenge C004-CH2.

Claims:
1. OsiguroMi identified duplicate records and incorrect timestamps among the data errors causing false payouts, and requires processing to complete within 60 seconds within existing infrastructure (C004-CH2, C004). [C004-CH2, C004]
2. Using the approximately 340,000 historical API records from OsiguroMi (C004-CH2), Predrag Nedić would design the deduplication and data-quality validation component of the validation layer—applying deterministic blocking and probabilistic field matching (SYN-PUB-10567, SYN-PUB-06833) to detect duplicate and erroneous records from the flight-status API feed—and ensure the pipeline meets the 60-second latency constraint within the existing Kubernetes deployment (SYN-PUB-10566, C004). 4. OsiguroMi tested simple rule-based anomaly detection and found it triggered too many false alarms, and identifies the need for a credibility or anomaly assessment method as the core gap (C004-CH2); Nedić's records cover stream processing pipeline architecture, latency optimisation, and Kubernetes deployment (SYN-PUB-10566, SYN-PUB-06833), not false-positive suppression or anomaly scoring methods. Review the claims of pair C004-CH2:R0571.
It is about: researcher Mirjana Malešević (R0571) and company OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004), challenge C004-CH2.

Claims:
1. Using ~340,000 historical API call and payout records from OsiguroMi (C004-CH2), Mirjana Malešević would design and deploy a streaming validation layer that detects duplicate records, misclassified cancellations, and timestamp anomalies in the FlightBridge feed before payouts fire (C004), applying anomaly scoring methods (SYN-PUB-06618, SYN-PUB-06615, SYN-PUB-06623) and field-level consistency checks (SYN-PUB-06616, SYN-PUB-06620) within the existing Kubernetes pipeline (C004), targeting a false-positive rate below the current 3.1% error rate (C004-CH2). [C004-CH2, C004, SYN-PUB-06618, SYN-PUB-06615, SYN-PUB-06623, SYN-PUB-06616, SYN-PUB-06620]

Sources:
[C004-CH2] challenge · We process around 9,000 travel-delay claims per month fully automatically, but our internal audit found that 3.1% of payouts were triggered by data errors from the flight-status API rather than genuine delays — that's real money leaking out every month. · company C004

To nije zanemarljiv procenat kad govorimo o isplatama u eurima. Trenutno radimo sa jednim eksternim API-jem za status letova. Review the claims of profile R0842.
It is about: researcher Péter Szabó (R0842).

Claims:
1. Led the work package on statistical methodology in CATTOOL, an applied project that produced a decision-support toolkit for small non-life insurers; implementation in R and Stan for Bayesian updating of catastrophe loss models. [SYN-PRJ-0117, SYN-PUB-09115]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-09115] publication · Bayesian updating of catastrophe loss models using sequential Monte Carlo · 2023 · researchers R0842
Bayesian updating of catastrophe loss models using sequential Monte Carlo (2023, journal, Computational Statistics and Data Analysis).
Authors: Marija Ivanović-Pešić (outside co-author); László Varga (outside co-author); Péter Szabó (R0842).
Keywords: sequential Monte Carlo; Bayesian updating; catastrophe modelling; GPD; hailstorm losses.
Catastrophe risk models for pricing and reserving are typically calibrated on datasets that are augmented by a new large event every several years. Re-running full MCMC after each such update is computationally costly. We adapt a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) scheme to propagate posterior distributions over GPD parameters as new catastrophe event observations arrive. Tempering schedules and resampling strategies are tuned for the low-event-count regime typical of natural catastrophe lines: 8 to 30 historical events. We apply the SMC scheme to a stylised hailstorm loss series for the Pannonian Plain region, simulating sequential arrival of one to three new events. Posterior contraction and shifts in 99th-percentile return-level estimates are documented. Computation time is compared with fresh MCMC runs. The approach is implemented in Stan with custom R wrappers.

Review the claims of profile R0422.
It is about: researcher Attila Bálint (R0422).

Claims:
1. Extreme value theory and spliced distributions for tail risk estimation in cyber loss data, including generalised Pareto distribution fitting and threshold selection. [SYN-PUB-05085, SYN-PUB-05074]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-05085] publication · Tail Risk Estimation for Cloud Service Outage Losses: A Spliced Distribution Approach with Application to Serbian Fintech Firms · 2026 · researchers R0422, R0970, R0671
Tail Risk Estimation for Cloud Service Outage Losses: A Spliced Distribution Approach with Application to Serbian Fintech Firms (2026, preprint, Preprint, SSRN Working Paper Series).
Authors: Nikola Savić (outside co-author); Milica Đorđević (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422); Rita Bálint (R0970); Emilija Ostojić (R0671).
Keywords: spliced distribution; cloud outage; generalised Pareto; fintech; business interruption.
Cloud service outages generate bimodal loss profiles: a large mass of short, low-cost interruptions and a thin tail of prolonged outages with severe financial consequences. This paper fits spliced distributions combining a gamma body with a generalised Pareto tail to hourly downtime cost data collected from 19 fintech firms operating in Serbia between 2021 and 2024, yielding 2 641 outage episodes. The splice point is selected by minimising the integrated squared error between the empirical CDF and the fitted spliced distribution, resulting in an optimal threshold at the 87th empirical percentile. The GPD shape parameter governing the tail is estimated at 0.38 (95% CI: 0.21–0.55), confirming heavy-tail behaviour. Annual aggregate loss distributions are constructed via compound Poisson simulation. The 99th-percentile annual outage loss for a median-sized firm is estimated at EUR 180 000, with high sensitivity to the GPD shape parameter. Probali smo da dopunimo bazu podacima iz otvorenih izvora i novinskih arhiva, ali kvalitet i doslednost su neujednačeni. Reconciling Conflicting Records from Heterogeneous Industrial Databases in Near-Real-Time (2020, journal, Journal of Industrial Data Integration).
Authors: Sorin Moldovan (outside co-author); Anita Vojvodić (outside co-author); Nemanja Grujić (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020).
Keywords: data reconciliation; entity resolution; change data capture; industrial databases; near-real-time.
Industrial environments often run multiple transactional databases that record overlapping facts about the same physical entities—machines, batches, or shipments—with differing update frequencies and inconsistent identifiers. We designed a reconciliation pipeline that ingests change-data-capture streams from three source databases simultaneously, performs entity resolution using a deterministic blocking scheme followed by probabilistic field matching, and produces a unified view updated with a median lag of 1.4 seconds. The system was evaluated on a dataset derived from a manufacturing scenario comprising approximately 2.1 million entity records and 11 months of change history, replayed at 5× real-time speed. Solid-state screening of ibuprofen co-formers selected by hydrogen-bond propensity calculations (2015, journal, Crystal Engineering and Materials Chemistry).
Authors: Lidija Radić (R0151); Marija Petrović (outside co-author); Adrián Fülöp (outside co-author).
Keywords: ibuprofen; co-crystal screening; hydrogen-bond propensity; dissolution rate; CSD.
Fourteen co-former candidates for ibuprofen were ranked using hydrogen-bond propensity (HBP) scores calculated from a Cambridge Structural Database subset of 1 200 entries containing carboxylic acid donors. The six highest-scoring candidates—nicotinamide, isonicotinamide, caffeine, l-proline, saccharin, and urea—were subjected to solution crystallisation, LAG, and spray-drying. PXRD, DSC, and solution-state ¹H NMR (DMSO-d₆) were used to confirm co-crystal formation. Three new co-crystalline phases were obtained: ibuprofen–isonicotinamide (2:1), ibuprofen–saccharin (1:1), and ibuprofen–l-proline (1:1). The ibuprofen–isonicotinamide co-crystal showed a 2.1-fold increase in intrinsic dissolution rate in pH 7.4 phosphate buffer and a powder flowability improvement (Carr index decreased from 28 to 19) relative to racemic ibuprofen. [SYN-PUB-05935] publication · Optimising corona-discharge parameters for heterogeneous recycled packaging boards using a response-surface approach · 2017 · researchers R0992, R0504
Optimising corona-discharge parameters for heterogeneous recycled packaging boards using a response-surface approach (2017, journal, Progress in Organic Coatings).
Authors: Miroslav Vujić (outside co-author); Đorđe Vukelić (R0992); Ljiljana Stanković (outside co-author); Tomáš Novák (outside co-author); Sanja Lukić (R0504).
Keywords: response surface methodology; corona discharge; recycled board; process optimisation; ink adhesion variability.
Recycled packaging boards sourced from three European mills exhibited substantial variability in initial surface energy (28–37 mJ/m²) due to differing furnish compositions and coating histories. A central composite response-surface design with four factors (electrode gap 1–3 mm, line speed 50–150 m/min, power density 5–20 W·min/m², ambient humidity 30–65 % RH) was used to model total surface energy and polar component as responses. Forty-three experimental runs were performed. The quadratic model explained 88 % of variance in total surface energy; power density and electrode gap were the dominant factors, with a statistically significant interaction. A validated optimal treatment window (gap 1.5 mm, 12 W·min/m², 40–55 % RH) yielded total surface energy ≥ 50 mJ/m² across all three board grades, reducing within-batch variability in ink adhesion peel force from ± 0.9 N/cm to ± 0.3 N/cm.

data.message:
Review the claims of profile R0750.
It is about: researcher István Lukács (R0750).

Claims:
1. Multi-criteria supplier selection using AHP and TOPSIS methods, applied to automotive and food processing supply chains. [SYN-PUB-03827]
2. Stochastic optimisation for supplier selection and order allocation under demand uncertainty, using two-stage models and scenario generation. [SYN-PUB-08279, SYN-PUB-08282]
3. Robust optimisation approaches for supplier selection when criteria weights are imprecisely specified, using min-max regret formulations. [SYN-PUB-08281]
4. Supply chain disruption risk quantification combining FMEA with Monte Carlo simulation to estimate annual disruption cost distributions. [SYN-PUB-08280]
5. Discrete-event simulation modelling of production lines for maintenance strategy comparison and buffer sizing optimisation. [SYN-PUB-01795, SYN-PUB-08283]
6. Implementation of optimisation and simulation models in MATLAB, Python, and AnyLogic. [R0750]
7. Integration of sustainability objectives—carbon emission penalties—into stochastic procurement models. [SYN-PUB-08282]
8. Open to joint projects with companies on supplier evaluation and procurement optimisation, contract research on supply chain risk modelling, and consulting on quantitative procurement decision support. [R0750]
9. Completed a four-month internship in logistics and procurement at a Novi Sad-based food packaging manufacturer during master's studies. [R0750]
10. Conducted structured interviews and data collection at eight Vojvodina SMEs in food processing and light manufacturing as part of the RISKCHAIN-VS project. [SYN-PRJ-0826]
11. Open to student internships involving data collection from industrial partners. [R0750]

data.message:
Review the claims of proposal C004-CH1-R0364.
It is about: researcher Žarko Pejić (R0364) and company OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004), challenge C004-CH1.

Claims:
1. OsiguroMi d.o.o. works in insurtech — embedded micro-insurance and parametric products. [C004]
2. Žarko Pejić is a Research Associate in the Remote Sensing and GIS Group, BioSense Institute. [R0364]
3. OsiguroMi's parametric payout trigger is based on the nearest official weather station, which can be up to 30 km from a farmer's parcel, and terrain variation means a drought signal at the station can coincide with local rain on the field, or vice versa. [C004-CH1]
4. The company holds access to RHMZS data and three private agro-meteorological networks totalling about 140 measurement points, but these have not yet been fused into a spatially continuous parcel-level rainfall product. [C004-CH1, C004]
5. The payout trigger is a fixed contractual threshold that cannot be replaced; the correction must come from more accurate spatial rainfall estimation at the parcel level. [C004-CH1]

Our biochar product tests at around 55% fixed carbon but customers in Germany need at least 70% for soil-amendment certification; we've tried raising pyrolysis temperature but that cuts yield by nearly a third and makes the economics fall apart.

Our biochar consistently comes out with around 55% fixed carbon when we run the pyrolyser at 500–520 °C, which is where our yield is commercially acceptable. Buyers in Germany and the Netherlands need at least 70% fixed carbon to qualify under soil-amendment certification schemes. We have pushed the temperature up to 650 °C and beyond in trials, and we do hit the 70% threshold, but the mass yield drops from roughly 28% to under 20%, which means we need about 40% more raw material to fill the same order. At current feedstock and energy costs that wipes out the price premium we get for certified biochar. We have also tried extending the hold time at lower temperatures rather than raising the peak, but the gains in fixed carbon are modest. Review the claims of pair C007-CH3:R0135.
It is about: researcher Veljko Savić (R0135) and company Suncokret Eko d.o.o. (C007), challenge C007-CH3.

Claims:
1. The challenge requires knowing how moisture and particle-size variance cause die clogging and bearing failures in a pellet press. [C007-CH3]
2. Savić co-authored work quantifying abrasive wear in pellet dies and ring-die geometry wear progression as functions of feedstock ash content and moisture. [SYN-PUB-01789, SYN-PUB-01785]
3. Savić led the RELIODENSE project, which developed a decision-support system combining NIR sensing with Bayesian degradation models and tested it at two commercial pellet facilities. [SYN-PRJ-0334]
4. Savić provided consulting to agricultural cooperatives in Vojvodina on maintenance programme restructuring for pellet production lines. [R0135]
5. Using quantitative models of pellet die and roller wear as functions of feedstock moisture and ash content, and the NIR-integrated decision-support system tested at commercial pellet facilities, define the moisture and particle-size tolerance window that keeps Suncokret Eko's press within safe operating limits, and evaluate whether the proposed hammer-mill and conditioning-mixer configuration would reliably hold incoming material within that window. [C007-CH3, SYN-PUB-01789, SYN-PUB-01785, SYN-PRJ-0334]
6. The published work covers wear modelling and condition monitoring of pellet press components; pre-processing equipment specification (hammer mill sizing, conditioning mixer configuration) is not within the scope of those records. [SYN-PUB-01789, SYN-PUB-01785, SYN-PRJ-0334]
7. The RELIODENSE NIR integration covers moisture monitoring for maintenance decisions; the challenge also requires particle-size characterisation, which is not covered in those records. [SYN-PRJ-0334, C007-CH3]

Sources:
[C007-CH3] challenge · Our pellet press breaks down about once a month because the sunflower husk feedstock has inconsistent moisture and particle size…[+8710 chars]

Review the claims of pair C007-CH3:R0750.
It is about: researcher István Lukács (R0750) and company Suncokret Eko d.o.o. (C007), challenge C007-CH3.

Claims:
1. The challenge involves fourteen suppliers delivering material with moisture ranging from 8% to 22%, and each breakdown costs approximately 15,000 EUR, creating a quantifiable disruption cost distribution. [C007-CH3, C007]
2. Lukács co-authored work on supply chain disruption risk quantification combining FMEA with Monte Carlo simulation to estimate annual disruption cost distributions. [SYN-PUB-08280]
3. Lukács co-authored stochastic optimisation models for supplier selection and order allocation under demand and quality uncertainty. [SYN-PUB-08279, SYN-PUB-08282]
4. Using stochastic supplier-selection and disruption-risk models applied to the fourteen-farm supply base, quantify the annual cost impact of feedstock quality variance from each supplier and identify which procurement allocation strategy would minimise quality-driven press downtime under the 1,200 tonne per year supply agreement. [C007-CH3, C007, SYN-PUB-08280, SYN-PUB-08279, SYN-PUB-08282]
5. The published work covers supplier selection and procurement optimisation in automotive and food processing supply chains; the records do not cover feedstock quality characterisation or pre-processing equipment specification for biomass densification. [SYN-PUB-03827, SYN-PUB-08279, SYN-PUB-08280]
6. The core difficulty requires defining the acceptable moisture and particle-size envelope and validating pre-processing equipment — this is a process-engineering question that the supplier-allocation models do not address. [C007-CH3]
7. The RISKCHAIN-VS project covered data collection at Vojvodina SMEs in food processing and light manufacturing; the records do not cover biomass or agricultural feedstock supply chains. [SYN-PRJ-0826]

Review the claims of profile R0151.
It is about: researcher Lidija Radić (R0151).

Claims:
1. Dissolution testing and solubility improvement of poorly soluble active pharmaceutical ingredients through polymorph and co-crystal selection, with measurement of intrinsic dissolution rate. [SYN-PUB-01957, SYN-PUB-01956, SYN-PUB-01952, SYN-PRJ-1392]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-01952] publication · Solid-state screening of ibuprofen co-formers selected by hydrogen-bond propensity calculations · 2015 · researchers R0151
Solid-state screening of ibuprofen co-formers selected by hydrogen-bond propensity calculations (2015, journal, Crystal Engineering and Materials Chemistry).
Authors: Lidija Radić (R0151); Marija Petrović (outside co-author); Adrián Fülöp (outside co-author).
Keywords: ibuprofen; co-crystal screening; hydrogen-bond propensity; dissolution rate; CSD.
Fourteen co-former candidates for ibuprofen were ranked using hydrogen-bond propensity (HBP) scores calculated from a Cambridge Structural Database subset of 1 200 entries containing carboxylic acid donors. The six highest-scoring candidates—nicotinamide, isonicotinamide, caffeine, l-proline, saccharin, and urea—were subjected to solution crystallisation, LAG, and spray-drying. PXRD, DSC, and solution-state ¹H NMR (DMSO-d₆) were used to confirm co-crystal formation. Three new co-crystalline phases were obtained: ibuprofen–isonicotinamide (2:1), ibuprofen–saccharin (1:1), and ibuprofen–l-proline (1:1). The ibuprofen–isonicotinamide co-crystal showed a 2.1-fold increase in intrinsic dissolution rate in pH 7.4 phosphate buffer and a powder flowability improvement (Carr index decreased from 28 to 19) relative to racemic ibuprofen. The HBP ranking correctly predicted three of four successful outcomes, supporting its utility as a pre-screening filter to reduce experimental effort. The ibuprofen–urea and ibuprofen–caffeine combinations gave only physical mixtures under all conditions tested.

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-01789] publication · Influence of sunflower husk ash content on abrasive wear rate of pellet die steel: a laboratory pin-on-disc study · 2019 · researchers R0135
Influence of sunflower husk ash content on abrasive wear rate of pellet die steel: a laboratory pin-on-disc study (2019, journal, Tribology in Industry).
Authors: Marija Stanković (outside co-author); Veljko Savić (R0135); Zoltán Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: abrasive wear; pellet die steel; sunflower husk; ash content; pin-on-disc.
Pin-on-disc wear tests were conducted on coupons of X46Cr13 die steel—the most common die material in Vojvodina pellet facilities—using abrasive slurries prepared from sunflower husk ash at five mass fractions: 0%, 2%, 5%, 10%, and 15%. Tests were run at a sliding speed of 0.3 m/s and a normal load of 20 N for 3,600 seconds each, with three replicates per condition. Mass loss was recorded gravimetrically at 600-second intervals. Specific wear rate increased from 1.4 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/N·m at 0% ash to 6.1 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/N·m at 15% ash. SEM micrographs of worn surfaces confirm a transition from ploughing-dominated to micro-cutting-dominated wear mechanisms above 5% ash content, correlated with an increase in angular silica particles in that fraction. The results provide quantitative input for updating the wear coefficient in maintenance scheduling models for pellet lines processing high-ash feedstocks. An empirical correction factor as a function of ash mass fraction is tabulated.

1. Comparative evaluation of fixed-interval, condition-based, and predictive maintenance strategies for pellet production lines using discrete-event simulation parameterised from field failure data. [SYN-PUB-01795]

Comparative evaluation of fixed-interval, condition-based, and predictive maintenance strategies for biomass pellet lines: a simulation study based on field failure data (2026, journal, International Journal of Production Research).
Authors: Veljko Savić (R0135); István Lukács (R0750); Ivana Petrović (outside co-author); Nemanja Vučković (outside co-author); Radovan Petrušić (outside co-author).
Keywords: discrete-event simulation; maintenance strategy comparison; pellet production line; availability; cost analysis.
A discrete-event simulation model of a full pellet production line—feed preparation, ring-die press, cooler, sieving, and bagging—was parameterised using failure and repair time distributions derived from 36 months of maintenance records from three commercial facilities in Vojvodina. Three maintenance strategies were compared: time-based fixed-interval (TBM), condition-based using a single vibration threshold (CBM), and predictive using the NIR-integrated RUL model developed in an earlier study (PM). Each strategy was evaluated over 10,000 simulated hours using 500 replications. Key performance indicators were line availability, number of unplanned stops, and total maintenance cost per tonne of product. A Weighted TOPSIS Approach for Supplier Selection in the Automotive Tier-2 Supply Chain: A Case Study from the Vojvodina Region (2022, journal, Journal of Industrial Engineering and Management (Novi Sad)).
Authors: István Lukács (R0750); Jelena Borozan (outside co-author); Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Mihály Varga (outside co-author); Đorđe Novaković (R0331).
Keywords: TOPSIS; AHP; supplier selection; automotive supply chain; sensitivity analysis.
This paper applies a weighted Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) model to evaluate and rank a set of 14 candidate suppliers for a Vojvodina-based automotive component manufacturer. Seven criteria were defined through structured interviews with procurement managers, covering price, delivery reliability, quality rejection rate, financial stability, geographic proximity, environmental certification, and responsiveness. Criteria weights were elicited using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with input from five domain experts. The consistency ratio for all pairwise comparison matrices remained below 0.08. Sensitivity analysis was performed by varying the weight of the top two criteria by ±20%. Results show that the final supplier ranking is stable under moderate weight perturbations, with the top three suppliers retaining their positions across all tested scenarios. data.message:
Review the claims of proposal C004-CH1-R0364.
It is about: researcher Žarko Pejić (R0364) and company OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004), challenge C004-CH1.

Claims:
1. Access to RHMZS data and three private agro-meteorological networks totalling about 140 measurement points across the region. [C004-CH1, C004]
2. A Python environment for actuarial modelling and trigger calibration, and PostgreSQL databases with time series for historical losses. [C004]
3. One internal researcher for data modelling and two senior engineers who can dedicate part of their capacity to joint projects. [C004]
4. Pejić co-authored burn analysis and basis risk assessment for crop index insurance across cadastral municipalities and sample parcels. [SYN-PUB-04462, SYN-PUB-04014]
5. Pejić co-authored ordinary kriging methods for monthly rainfall mapping and a Bayesian kriging approach for merging gauge and satellite precipitation data. [SYN-PUB-04460, SYN-PUB-04463]
6. OsiguroMi's payout trigger is based on official stations up to 30 km from a farmer's parcel, and the goal is to correct payout logic through more accurate spatial estimation without replacing the contractual threshold. [C004-CH1]
7. Pejić co-authored a kriging-with-external-drift method blending IMERG satellite estimates with gauge networks to produce field-scale rainfall grids. [SYN-PUB-04461]

Review the claims of profile R0920.
It is about: researcher Filip Urošević (R0920).

Claims:
1. Tool life modelling for CrAlN-coated inserts using a modified Taylor equation with feed rate as a secondary variable, validated across multiple cutting speeds and feed rates for hardened steel. [SYN-PUB-09761]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-09761] publication · Tool life modelling for CrAlN-coated inserts in high-speed dry turning using a modified Taylor equation · 2021 · researchers R0920, R1041
Tool life modelling for CrAlN-coated inserts in high-speed dry turning using a modified Taylor equation (2021, journal, CIRP Journal of Manufacturing Science and Technology).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920); Gordana Zorić (R1041); Ákos Horvát (outside co-author).
Keywords: Taylor tool life; CrAlN; dry turning; tool life model; hardened steel.
Tool life data for CrAlN-coated WC-Co inserts turning AISI 4340 steel (48 HRC) were collected at six cutting speeds (120–320 m/min) and three feed rates (0.08, 0.12 and 0.16 mm/rev), depth fixed at 0.5 mm, in strictly dry conditions. VB = 0.3 mm was used as the failure criterion. Ninety-six complete tool life tests were conducted with three replicates per condition. A modified Taylor equation incorporating feed rate as a secondary variable was fitted by nonlinear least squares; the exponents were n = 0.31 and m = 0.48 for speed and feed, respectively, with standard errors below 5 %. A validation set of 12 tests at intermediate conditions gave mean absolute percentage error of 9.2 %. The model was also compared against a response surface regression (second-order); both achieved similar predictive accuracy, but the Taylor-based form offers better extrapolation behaviour outside the experimental range.

Our pellet press breaks down about once a month because the sunflower husk feedstock has inconsistent moisture and particle size coming from different suppliers; downtime costs us roughly 15,000 EUR per incident when we have delivery commitments.

Our pellet press line goes down roughly once a month. The root cause is almost always the same: sunflower husk material arriving with moisture content or particle size outside the range the press can handle. When moisture is above 14% the dies clog; when there is too much fine dust mixed with coarser pieces the compression is uneven and we get bearing failures. Different suppliers deliver material that can vary from 8% to 22% moisture and from fine powder to chunks over 15 mm in the same delivery. Our current process is to check a sample at intake and reject loads that look bad, but our in-line NIR sensor only covers moisture and is not reliable below 10% or above 18%, and we have no automated particle-size check at all. Each breakdown costs us around 15,000 EUR in lost production, emergency maintenance and contract penalties. Review the claims of profile R0308.
It is about: researcher Jovan Bogićević (R0308).

Claims:
1. Leads work package 3 on press-brake digital twin design and sensor integration for the FORMTWIN international collaborative project with academic and SME partners. [SYN-PRJ-0591]

Sources:
[SYN-PRJ-0591] project · Digital Twin Architectures for Sheet-Metal Forming Machines in SME Environments · 2023 · researchers R0308, R0377
FORMTWIN: Digital Twin Architectures for Sheet-Metal Forming Machines in SME Environments (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0308 work package leader; R0377 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Kragujevac; Department of Manufacturing Science and Technology, Budapest University of Technology and Economics; Institute for Logistics and Production Systems, University of Miskolc; Metaloform d.o.o., Novi Sad; Acélszerkezet Kft., Győr; Lemezipari Zrt., Debrecen.
FORMTWIN brings together two Serbian and two Hungarian academic institutions with three SME partners operating sheet-metal job shops to develop practically deployable digital twin prototypes for press-brake and stamping machines. Bogićević leads Work Package 3, covering press-brake digital twin design, sensor integration, and FEM-based state estimation. The work package is producing a reference instrumentation kit (sensor selection, mounting guidelines, data-acquisition hardware) that the SME partners are piloting on their production machines. Deliverables include a software framework released under an open licence, two joint journal publications, and a training workshop held at the Science Technology Park Novi Sad. The project runs until mid-2026.

Review the claims of proposal C004-CH1-R0364.
It is about: researcher Žarko Pejić (R0364) and company OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004), challenge C004-CH1.

Claims:
1. Pejić co-authored burn analysis and basis risk assessment for crop index insurance across cadastral parcels, the calibration step needed to measure whether the corrected grid reduces incorrect payouts. [SYN-PUB-04462, SYN-PUB-04014]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-04462] publication · Design of a Rainfall Deficit Index for Maize Insurance in the Vojvodina Region: Sensitivity to Spatial Resolution of Input Precipitation Grids · 2020 · researchers R0364
Design of a Rainfall Deficit Index for Maize Insurance in the Vojvodina Region: Sensitivity to Spatial Resolution of Input Precipitation Grids (2020, journal, Journal of Agricultural Risk and Finance).
Authors: Ljubica Ristić (outside co-author); Nataša Filipović (outside co-author); Marco Ceriani (outside co-author); Žarko Pejić (R0364).
Keywords: rainfall deficit index; basis risk; maize insurance; CHIRPS; ERA5; DSSAT.
Index insurance products that trigger payouts based on area-average rainfall can suffer from basis risk when the spatial resolution of the underlying precipitation data does not capture field-level variability. This study quantified how the choice of precipitation grid resolution (0.25°, 0.05°, and 1 km downscaled) affects the properties of a 30-day rainfall deficit index (RDI) designed for rainfed maize in Vojvodina. Historical RDI series were reconstructed for 1995–2018 using ERA5 reanalysis at 0.25°, CHIRPS at 0.05°, and a KED-downscaled product at 1 km. Basis risk was approximated by computing the correlation between field-scale simulated crop water deficits from a DSSAT maize model and each RDI series for 120 sample parcels. Pearson correlation with the 1 km RDI was 0.71, versus 0.58 for CHIRPS and 0.49 for ERA5. Trigger and exit thresholds calibrated on the 1 km product changed payout frequency by up to 18 percentage points compared with coarser inputs.…[+1916 chars]

Our sheet-metal enclosure workshop in Subotica produces around 2,400 panels a year; we bend and weld everything in-house but we are seeing a 6% rework rate on powder-coated parts because weld spatter creates surface defects that only appear after coating — we lose roughly 140,000 dinars per month in rework labour and materials.

Our panel enclosures go through MIG welding before powder coating, and we have a persistent rework problem. Weld spatter — tiny metal balls that stick to the sheet surface — is not always visible before the part goes into the coating oven. After coating the spatter shows up as raised bumps or pinholes and the part has to be stripped, re-ground, re-primed, and re-coated. We track rework per batch and the rate has sat at around 6% for three years. That translates to roughly 140,000 dinars a month in extra labour and materials, not counting the scheduling delays when a batch comes back. We have tried tightening welding parameters, switching to an anti-spatter spray, and adding a manual inspection step before priming, but the manual check catches maybe half the defective parts. Review the claims of proposal C007-CH1-R0992.
It is about: researcher Đorđe Vukelić (R0992) and company Suncokret Eko d.o.o. (C007), challenge C007-CH1.

Claims:
1. Suncokret Eko d.o.o. works in cleantech — biomass and organic waste valorisation. [C007]
2. Đorđe Vukelić is an Associate Professor in the Department of Applied and Engineering Chemistry, Faculty of Technology. [R0992]
3. Suncokret Eko's batch pyrolysis of sunflower husks and maize cobs runs at 500–520°C, producing biochar with 55% fixed carbon at 28% mass yield. [C007-CH1]
4. Customers in Germany and the Netherlands require 70% fixed carbon for soil-amendment certification; raising temperature to 650°C meets the threshold but drops mass yield below 20%. [C007-CH1]
5. A mass yield below 20% requires 40% more feedstock per order, eliminating the price premium the certified product commands. [C007-CH1]
6. Feedstock arrives from different suppliers with variable moisture and particle size, adding process variability the company has not yet quantified. [C007-CH3]
7. A 2023 study reports an RSM model that predicts biochar yield from fixed carbon content, reaction temperature, and heating rate, developed on a Box-Behnken design across three biomass types. [W4319953064]
8. A batch slow-pyrolysis reactor with a 400–700°C operating range, two years of production logs covering temperature profiles, feedstock moisture, particle size, and output quality. [C007, C007-CH1]
9. Two technically trained staff who can run controlled production trials and maintain detailed process logs, available for trial execution throughout the project. [C007]
10. In-house proximate and ultimate analysis capability for biochar (fixed carbon, ash, volatile matter). [C007]
11. Baseline performance data: 28% mass yield and 55% fixed carbon at 500–520°C. [C007-CH1]

Review the claims of profile R0811.
It is about: researcher Branislava Janković (R0811).

Claims:
1. Link budget analysis for LoRa deployments in dense urban areas and challenging propagation environments including seasonal foliage effects. [SYN-PUB-08826, SYN-PUB-08822, SYN-PUB-08820]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-08826] publication · LoRa Link Budget Analysis for Water Meter Telemetry in a Dense Urban Area: A Case Study · 2020 · researchers R0962, R0811
LoRa Link Budget Analysis for Water Meter Telemetry in a Dense Urban Area: A Case Study (2020, book chapter, IoT Deployment Strategies for Smart Cities – Edited Volume, TechPress Balkan).
Authors: Ljiljana Stanković (outside co-author); Danilo Uzelac (R0962); Branislava Janković (R0811).
Keywords: water metering; AMR; link budget; basement deployment; LoRaWAN.
This chapter examines the practical link budget constraints encountered when deploying LoRaWAN-based automatic meter reading for water utilities in a densely built urban district. The case study is based on a pilot deployment of 340 end nodes in the Stari Grad neighbourhood of Novi Sad, where meter boxes are located in basement utility cupboards 1.5–2.5 m below street level. The chapter first derives an extended link budget model that accounts for: outdoor urban path loss (measured empirically), building wall penetration loss (14–28 dB depending on construction type), and meter-box cavity shielding (estimated 6–10 dB additional loss). The model is validated against measured delivery rates from the pilot. Results show that SF10 was sufficient for 87% of nodes, while the remaining 13% required SF12 and in some cases external antenna cables. Network dimensioning guidelines are provided for practitioners.
